### Policy-side notes (not KB verdicts)
- PN1 (dangling parameters). The overwrites retire the clauses that read `add_on_fees_follow_nightly` and `service_fee_partial_refund_mode`, but the variants and the parameter schema keep both with normative descriptions. The KB renders them faithfully in `in_stay_and_component_refund_settings_884c86b6` ("Pet fee and extra-guest fee refunded in the same proportion as the nightly subtotal | Yes"; "How the guest service fee is refunded outside the full-refund window | proportional"), next to the component ledger standard that retires the clauses reading them. A careful reader reconciles them (the blind pass did), but a support agent sees an unqualified setting that the current rules override for monthly and pay-part-now stays. Origin: policy side; realism cost.
- PN2 (placement). The cancellation-fee policy `stay_ext_departure_service_fee_refund` overwrites the travel-issue approval/reporting-window and MDE approval clauses, so their in-force wording lives only in the guest-service-fee-on-cancellation hub while the travel-issue and MDE documents show them as "no longer in force as worded". Faithful rendering; realism cost (a reader of travel-issue rules is sent to a cancellation document for the eligibility conditions).
- PN3. Rule text "This covers a guest who leaves a long stay paid month by month before the installments reach the nights the cancellation keeps …" is source wording that describes this task's situation class; rendered verbatim.
- PN4. The four refund rules say the credit-funded part "goes back as credits"; no write for returning credits exists in this product's tools, and the GT performs none. Policy-side scope note.
- Cross-product (outside criterion range): stay documents say "dedicated concierge" / "priority support line"; the Rewards chart (runtime KB, product `rewards`) says "Named concierge" / "Priority guest support line". The mapping was made without difficulty.

## dependency_form

Scan of the whole `docs/stay` corpus against the blind hop marks (all five hops state-derived, none pre-solved):
- Prerequisite sentences: each stands verbatim, state form, only in the hub of the policy it blocks; the two "Read against the stay's ledger: …" sentences are same-form restatements in the same hubs, listing that hub's own waited-on states, not a chain across hops.
- State-form sentence restated as an action, another problem's tool name, policy id, route, ordered step list across problems, dependency table/checklist/roadmap, "if unmet, first …" guidance: none found (tool names occur only in their own documents; searched "first call", "before calling", "then call", "refer to", "see the").
- Depended-on documents (pet-fee, extra-guest-fee, GSF hubs) never disclose who waits on them, and are reachable through the records' and the sentences' own words ("pet fee", "extra-guest fee", "guest service fee", "refund", "ledger").
- Titles/openings: general subjects (e.g. "Notice Charge on a Stay Cancelled in Progress", "Pet-Fee Refund on a Guest Cancellation"); none mirrors this task. The hub's "This covers …" sentence is source text (PN3), not a rendering addition.
- Computation documents: no hint of variation ("unless otherwise", "adjustments", "certain customers", pointers) — none found in the four computation documents.
- Factor documents: none states which tier a customer falls on or names the computation document. One item examined and not recorded as RED: `returning_guest_relief_on_departure_charge_fee_50181cb3` Q&A "What happens when the fee also carries another relief? … With a returning-guest relief of 25 percent and another relief of 50 percent, 75 percent … with another relief of 100 percent, the total is held at the whole fee." The acknowledgement of a second relief is forced by the source's own sentence "The two reliefs are added together, never relieve more than the whole fee …", which the KB must carry; the document does not name the other relief, its document or its evidence, and the solver still has to reach the Rewards relief through the Rewards membership record. The 50 / 100 example figures coincide with the Rewards relief's tiers; recorded here as a watch item, not as a routing statement.

**PASS**
